newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish KGHM sees its offer unhurt by other issues.
newsitem.headline: Polish KGHM sees its offer unhurt by other issues.

text.p: The public offering of Poland's KGHM Polska Miedz SA copper concern, which starts on June 30, should not suffer from any other issues including that of Bank Handlowy, KGHM's deputy president said on Friday.
Asked whether the issue of state-owned Bank Handlowy SA just before KGHM hits the market might not divert investors' interest, Jerzy Dobrzanski told a news conference:
"Large public offerings should not affect the sale of KGHM shares because our company is different from banks and investors will perceive us differently."
Up to 36 percent of KGHM, valued at a total of 3.0-4.6 billion zlotys, goes on sale just two weeks after the big-ticket sale closes of Bank Handlowy, which is valued at up to 3.25 billion zlotys.
Handlowy's public offer is worth about one billion zlotys.
KGHM expects to attract foreign financial institutions, Dobrzanski told the conference devoted to environmental issues in the region around Legnica in southwest Poland where KGHM is located.
"Foreign investors are analysing KGHM very closely and there are some which have been awaiting this offer," he said.
Dobrzanski said KGHM expected a 15-percent free tranche reserved for the firm's present and former employees to be fully taken up.
"There are about 45,000 people entitled to employee shares and it seems that the whole batch will be be used up," he said.
